sources.section: File Transfer - Object Storage & File Servers
sources.entry: s3-orchestrator - Storage orchestration layer presenting many cloud providers as a single S3 endpoint, keeping N copies across them with read failover, plus optional per-backend byte, request, ingress and egress limits, zstd compression and envelope encryption. (Source Code) MIT Go/Docker/deb/K8S

summary.one_liner: s3-orchestrator is a Go service that presents several S3-compatible storage backends (OCI, Backblaze B2, AWS S3, MinIO, Wasabi, Cloudflare R2, etc.) as one S3 endpoint, tracking object locations in its own database.
summary.what_it_does: Puts a single S3 endpoint in front of multiple S3-compatible backends and exposes them as one or more virtual buckets. It records where each object lives in its own metadata store (embedded SQLite or PostgreSQL, with Redis-backed shared counters for multi-instance deployments). It enforces per-backend byte quotas with overflow to the next backend, and optional monthly request, ingress and egress caps. It can keep N copies of each object across distinct backends, fail reads over to a surviving copy, and run a scrubber that checks stored bytes against recorded hashes. Operators can cordon and drain backends, rebalance, import an existing bucket, and use a web dashboard, admin API and hot config reload.
use_cases: Combine free-tier allocations from several providers into one bucket
Add automatic cloud redundancy to a local MinIO instance
Keep multiple replicas of objects across different cloud providers
Migrate from one S3 provider to another without downtime
Encrypt and compress objects at rest across cloud backends
Manage buckets, users and grants with Terraform
how_to_run: aws --endpoint-url <orchestrator endpoint> s3 cp /etc/hostname s3://photos/test.txt (after make run, endpoint at localhost:9000)
notable: Replication via parallel_copies: writes upload to all targets at once and answer on the first committed copy, reducing replicator GETs and source egress
Per-backend byte, request, ingress and egress limits that let several small free-tier allocations act as one larger bucket
Backends see only plain S3 calls, so no changes are needed on the provider side
Envelope encryption with keys inline, in a file, or in Vault Transit; compression runs before encryption
Online backend drain and over-replication trimming for moving providers without downtime
caveats: Multi-instance deployments require PostgreSQL; SQLite is for single-instance use
Quickstart requires Go 1.27+, Docker and Make
The README's comparison table notes MinIO Gateway is deprecated and that rclone union works client-side, so this is a server-side design choice rather than a drop-in for every use
Flexify.IO is a commercial alternative mentioned by the README; this project is MIT-licensed
